display.purpose: The two team names in the board's spotlight. The largest words on any screen, scaled with the viewport so one panel serves a phone and a venue display.

headline.purpose: Admin page titles. Drops from 2rem to 1.5rem below 900px.

title.purpose: Card and panel headings across both themes.

body.purpose: All prose. 17px rather than 16 because it is read outdoors at arm's length; hints drop to 0.92rem and measure no wider than 60ch.

label.purpose: Column headers, time headings, nav groups, tags, board panel titles. The only role permitted to be uppercase, and never above 0.92rem.

mono.purpose: Join codes and admin-issued temporary passwords. Keeps 0 apart from O while somebody reads one out across a car park. The system's only monospace, and a code is the only thing that earns it.

score.purpose: The spotlight scoreline and every figure that can change. Tabular figures at every size so digits never shift as a score updates.

shadows.name: admin-lift
shadows.purpose: The only shadow in the light theme. Lets admin panels drop their border entirely so definition comes from whitespace.

shadows.name: glass-lift
shadows.purpose: Every board panel. The inset highlight is the light-catching top edge that makes a translucent sheet read as physical.

shadows.name: glass-live
shadows.purpose: The spotlight while a match is running. The only state-driven shadow in the system.

motion.name: press
motion.purpose: Every button on :active. The whole system's click feel; there is no other press treatment.

motion.name: caret
motion.purpose: The admin nav's disclosure caret rotating 90deg on open.

motion.name: progress
motion.purpose: The day's progress bar filling. Suppressed under prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: pulse
motion.purpose: The live dot inside a live tag. The only looping animation in the system, and suppressed entirely under prefers-reduced-motion.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The end of a task, so it spans the column. Navy fill, 48px minimum for a gloved thumb.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { font: 700 17px/1.45 Poppins, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif; width: 100%; min-height: 48px; padding: 0 1rem; background: var(--brand, #00467f); color: #fff; border: 1px solid var(--brand, #00467f); border-radius: var(--radius, 10px); cursor: pointer; touch-action: manipulation; } .ds-btn-primary:active { transform: translateY(1px); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid var(--focus, #f5c518); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-btn-primary:disabled { opacity: 0.5; cursor: not-allowed; }

components.name: Score Stepper
components.description: The primary scoring control. A 48px square with a 1.6rem glyph, flanking a tabular score.
components.html: 2
components.css: .ds-stepper { display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 0.5rem; } .ds-step { width: 48px; min-height: 48px; padding: 0; font: 700 1.6rem/1 Poppins, -apple-system, sans-serif; background: #fff; color: #1a1d21; border: 1px solid #dfe4e9; border-radius: 10px; cursor: pointer; touch-action: manipulation; } .ds-step:active { transform: translateY(1px); } .ds-step:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid #f5c518; outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-step-value { min-width: 3.1rem; text-align: center; font: 800 2.6rem/1 Poppins, -apple-system, sans-serif; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; color: #1a1d21; }

components.name: Card Buttons
components.description: Yellow and red cards, set below a rule with 1.5rem of clearance from the score steppers. A mis-tap books a player who did nothing, so the separation is structural.
components.css: .ds-card-buttons { display: flex; gap: 0.6rem; justify-content: center; margin-top: 1.5rem; padding-top: 1rem; border-top: 1px solid #dfe4e9; } .ds-card-buttons button { flex: 1 1 0; min-width: 0; min-height: 48px; padding: 0 1rem; font: 700 17px/1.45 Poppins, -apple-system, sans-serif; border-radius: 10px; cursor: pointer; touch-action: manipulation; } .ds-btn-yellow { background: #f7d154; border: 1px solid #d9b23f; color: #1a1d21; } .ds-btn-red { background: #c0392b; border: 1px solid #c0392b; color: #fff; } .ds-card-buttons button:active { transform: translateY(1px); } .ds-card-buttons button:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid #f5c518; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Kit Card
components.description: The light theme's container: white on grey, one hairline, no shadow. A live game thickens the border to 2px navy — depth never means state.

components.name: Admin Panel
components.description: The desk theme: borderless and roomy, floating on a two-layer ambient shadow. Definition comes from whitespace rather than hard edges.

components.name: Glass Panel
components.description: The board's container. 7.5% white over deep navy, 22px backdrop blur, a translucent edge and a 1px inset highlight along the top — the light-catching edge that makes it read as a physical sheet.

components.css: .ds-spotlight { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1fr auto 1fr; align-items: center; gap: 0.9rem; padding: 1.3rem 1.4rem 1.15rem; background: linear-gradient(163deg, #0d2542 0%, #071829 100%); border: 1px solid rgba(227, 24, 55, 0.45); border-radius: 16px; box-shadow: 0 12px 40px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.34), 0 0 0 1px rgba(227, 24, 55, 0.18), inset 0 1px 0 rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.16); } .ds-spot-team { min-width: 0; display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: center; text-align: center; } .ds-spot-name { font: 600 clamp(1.35rem, 2.4vw, 2rem)/1.15 'Lubalin Graph', Rockwell, 'Roboto Slab', Georgia, serif; color: #fff; overflow-wrap: anywhere; } .ds-spot-numbers { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.85rem; } .ds-spot-n { font: 800 clamp(2.6rem, 6vw, 4.1rem)/1 Poppins, -apple-system, sans-serif; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; letter-spacing: -0.03em; color: #fff; } .ds-spot-sep { width: 14px; height: 2px; border-radius: 2px; background: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.66); }

components.name: Live Tag
components.description: The board's status marker. Only a running match wears SCORES Red, and its dot is the system's only looping animation.
components.css: .ds-tag { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.35rem; padding: 0.2rem 0.6rem; border-radius: 999px; font: 700 0.74rem/1.2 Poppins, -apple-system, sans-serif; letter-spacing: 0.03em; text-transform: uppercase; background: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.13); border: 1px solid rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.155); color: #fff; white-space: nowrap; } .ds-tag--live { background: var(--accent, #e31837); border-color: transparent; } .ds-tag--ghost { background: transparent; color: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.66); font-weight: 600; } .ds-dot { width: 7px; height: 7px; border-radius: 50%; background: currentColor; flex: 0 0 auto; animation: ds-pulse 1.9s ease-in-out infinite; } @keyframes ds-pulse { 0%, 100% { opacity: 1; transform: scale(1); } 50% { opacity: 0.35; transform: scale(0.72); } } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-dot { animation: none; } }

components.name: Text Field
components.description: White fill, hairline, 48px minimum. Focus is a ring rather than a border shift, because a ring survives sunlight where a 1px hue change does not.
components.css: .ds-field { margin-bottom: 0.9rem; } .ds-label { display: block; font: 600 0.85rem/1.45 Poppins, -apple-system, sans-serif; color: #5c6670; margin-bottom: 0.3rem; } .ds-input { font: 400 17px/1.45 Poppins, -apple-system, sans-serif; width: 100%; min-height: 48px; padding: 0 0.75rem; border: 1px solid #dfe4e9; border-radius: 10px; background: #fff; color: #1a1d21; } .ds-input:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid #f5c518; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Schedule Slot
components.description: A game on the admin grid. The 3px left edge carries the state: navy scheduled, red for a clash that must be fixed, dashed amber for no referee named.
components.css: .ds-slots { display: flex; gap: 0.5rem; flex-wrap: wrap; } .ds-slot { display: block; min-width: 11rem; text-align: left; min-height: 52px; padding: 0.35rem 0.45rem; border: 1px solid #dfe4e9; border-left: 3px solid var(--brand, #00467f); border-radius: 6px; background: #fff; cursor: pointer; line-height: 1.25; font-family: Poppins, -apple-system, sans-serif; } .ds-slot:hover { background: #f4f8fc; } .ds-slot:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid #f5c518; outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-slot--clash { border-left-color: #c0392b; background: #fdecea; } .ds-slot-teams { display: block; font-weight: 700; font-size: 0.84rem; color: #1a1d21; } .ds-slot-meta { display: block; font-size: 0.74rem; color: #5c6670; } .ds-slot-ref { display: block; font-size: 0.7rem; color: #5c6670; margin-top: 0.15rem; } .ds-slot-ref--none { color: #b8860b; font-style: italic; }

narrative.overview:
One Saturday in August, from the first kickoff to the last whistle. The system is built around the two things that actually happen on that day: a crowd standing in the sun wanting to know what just happened, and a volunteer with one free hand recording it. Everything else is downstream of those two moments.

So the system runs two faces of one identity. The board is the floodlit face — a deep navy field, frosted panels, scores large enough to read across a tent, a live match holding the top of the screen. The kit is the working face — white, hairline-ruled, 48-pixel targets because referees wear gloves, high contrast because the screen is being read at arm's length in direct sun. They are not two brands. They are the same navy, the same red, the same pencil yellow, arranged for two different jobs. Glass only reads well over a deep background, and a referee squinting at a phone in August daylight needs precisely the opposite of glass.

The personality is a sporting authority that never oversells: the numbers are the drama, so the interface does not compete with them. Density is generous on the board and compact in the kit. Ornament earns its place by encoding something real — a hatched fill means nobody has scored that game yet, a pulsing dot means a match is running now, a shirt icon means that is literally the shirt to look for on the pitch. Nothing decorative is allowed to look like data.
keyCharacteristics: Two themes, one palette: floodlit board, sunlit kit.
Numbers set in tabular figures at every size; digits never shift as scores change.
Red means now or wrong — never merely "important".
Definition from hairlines and whitespace in the kit, from depth and light-catching edges on the board.
Touch targets never below 48px in the field; 42px at a desk.
Every state that matters has a visible form, including absence: no field, no referee, no score.

rules.name: The Red Means Now Rule
rules.body: SCORES Red marks a match in progress and nothing else. If a thing is merely important, it is navy or it is bold — not red. A board where three panels are red is a board where nobody can find the game being played.

rules.name: The Pencil Yellow Rule
rules.body: Yellow is focus and following. It never fills a surface, never carries a label, and never appears as a brand accent. Its one decorative appearance — a 9%-opacity wash in the board's bottom glow — is the limit, not a precedent.

rules.name: The Cards Are Not A Palette Rule
rules.body: Card Yellow and Alarm Red belong to the referee's cards. No button, badge, or status may borrow them for an unrelated meaning; on this product a yellow rectangle is a booking.

rules.name: The Thirteen Steps Rule
rules.body: A size that is not on the ramp does not exist. The stylesheets once held 27 distinct sizes, fifteen of them between 0.68 and 0.98rem — differences of a third of a pixel that nobody chose and nobody could see. When a new element needs to sit between two steps, it takes one of them.

rules.name: The Numbers Are Not Decoration Rule
rules.body: Every figure that can change — scores, goals for and against, points, card counts, stat tiles, counters — sets in the body face with tabular figures. The display face never touches a changing number. A score that shifts sideways when 9 becomes 10 is a score people stop trusting.

rules.name: The No Shouting Rule
rules.body: The organisation's own site uses no uppercase runs, and neither does this. Uppercase belongs to labels at 0.92rem or below, always with positive tracking, never longer than three words. Headings are mixed case at every level, including in the admin.

rules.name: The Dash Is A Value Rule
rules.body: "–" means nobody has entered a score; "0" means it finished nil–nil. They must never render alike. An unentered figure is Soft Ink; an entered zero is full Ink at full weight.

rules.name: The Page Never Scrolls Sideways Rule
rules.body: Wide content scrolls inside its own container, never the document. Every grid column is minmax(0, 1fr), never a bare 1fr — 1fr's automatic minimum is min-content, so one wide table stretches the whole column past the screen instead of scrolling within it.

rules.name: The One Screen Rule
rules.body: At 1280px and above, the board fits one display with no scrolling. Anything added to it must earn its height from something else, not from the bottom of the page.

rules.name: The Material Changes, The Design Does Not Rule
rules.body: Bright sun may remove translucency, blur, gradient and glow, and may raise a tone or a type step. It may not move an element, change a colour's meaning, hide content, or introduce a shape the standard board does not have. Somebody switching mid-match must find the same board, in a different material.

rules.name: The One Mechanism Rule
rules.body: A surface is defined by a hairline, or by a shadow, or by glass. Never two. A bordered card with a drop shadow means someone has mixed the themes.

rules.name: The Blur Retreats In Daylight Rule
rules.body: Below 880px the glass gets more opaque (82% navy) and less blurred (12px), because blur is expensive and least legible exactly where phones are used — outdoors. Where backdrop-filter is unsupported, panels fall back to 90% solid navy. Translucency is never allowed to degrade into unreadable text.

rules.name: The Radius Follows Size Rule
rules.body: Small surfaces take small corners. A 6px radius on a 16px-tall control and a 16px radius on a full panel are the same gesture at two scales; a 16px radius on a small control is a different design.

dos: Do keep the two themes whole. Light surfaces for the referee, participant, and admin views; the glass board only over the navy gradient, scoped under .spectator.
Do set every changing number in tabular figures, at every size.
Do give absence a visible form — an Unassigned row for a game with no pitch, italic amber for a missing referee, a hatch for an unscored game, nothing at all for an unknown kit.
Do hold 48px touch targets in anything a referee uses outdoors, and 42px in the admin.
Do put the Pencil Yellow focus ring on every interactive element in both themes, at 3px with 2px offset.
Do let wide tables scroll inside .table-scroll, and write grid columns as minmax(0, 1fr).
Do state the consequence rather than the input — "35-minute slots → 9:00, 9:35, 10:10" beats three number fields.
Do suppress the pulse and the progress transition under prefers-reduced-motion.
donts: Don't put glass, blur, or the dark theme into the referee, participant, or admin views. Glass needs a deep background; a phone in August sun needs the opposite.
Don't use SCORES Red for anything but a live match, or Alarm Red for anything but an error, a clash, or a red card.
Don't borrow Card Yellow or the card shapes for unrelated UI states.
Don't render an unentered score as 0, or an entered 0 in the unentered treatment.
Don't combine a hairline border and a drop shadow on the same surface.
Don't set a heading, sentence, or button label in uppercase; uppercase stops at 0.92rem labels.
Don't set the display face on a number that can change.
Don't hide a game to filter a view — dim it. A hidden game is a game whose pitch clash nobody can see.
Don't add height to the board above 1280px without taking it from somewhere else; the page does not scroll there.
Don't rely on source order to win a CSS conflict in this project. Both the admin shell and the spectator board deliberately win on specificity, and the stylesheet says so in three places.
